Hi Sofia — thanks for sharing the redlines. I reviewed MiraHealth_DPA_redlines_v1.docx and highlighted the clauses that require discussion. High-level summary below plus embedded notes in the attached redline (separate stub).

Summary:
- Roles: Redwood confirms processor status. The customer's proposed language that attempts to shift certain obligations (broad "controller-style" instructions around ML model training and retention beyond agreed scope) is not acceptable as written. We're willing to add explicit language clarifying customer instructions and limited processing for model improvement only with opt-in and a documented purpose.
- SCCs: we will execute the EU Commission SCCs (2021 set) via an addendum for cross-border transfers. We will provide the completed Annex I-II mapping as part of the transfer impact addendum (TIA). Expect a short worksheet from us within 5 business days.
- BYOK / KMS: we support customer-managed keys in Private — options: (1) Customer KMS + Redwood HSM-wrapping (recommended), (2) Dedicated Redwood HSM with customer key escrow (less common). BYOK requires an additional Ops security runbook and limited onboarding window. It is allowed but classified as a paid professional services and recurring security maintenance line item.

Open items and positions:
1) Subprocessors: we maintain a standard subprocessor list and provide 30 days notice for new subprocessors. If MiraHealth needs prior approval for a particular subprocessor (e.g., we route inference through a partner in APAC), we can add a clause to require notice and escalation rather than blanket prior approval.
2) Data retention and export: the customer redline that requires deletion of logs within 30 days is an operational blocker for debugging/forensics. We can offer a compromise: default 90-day logs retention with scoped access controls and an option to shorten to 30 days at an increased cost and reduced observability SLA.
3) Audit evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II reports and targeted export-control attestations, and we will include a list of transfer safeguards in the TIA.

I've attached a legal redline PDF stub: [Redwood_DPA_response_redline.pdf]. Karthik — see item 2 and BYOK note below; please confirm the ops charge estimate and any latency/cost impacts for BYOK (key wrapping) so we can give procurement a ballpark.

Thanks,

Thanks Irene / Ben / Sofia — quick technical & commercial context from Infra: 
- BYOK (customer-managed KMS) is supported for our Private VPC package. Implementation steps: key trust setup, limited API changes to enable key-id routing, onboarding runbook, and quarterly key rotation guidance. Typical onboarding is 2-4 weeks of eng + security time.
- Latency: negligible for normal inference, <2% additional P95 token latency for HSM unwrap on cold-starts, not material.
- Cost model: we propose a two-part charge: one-time onboarding (professional services) of USD 8,000–12,000 and a monthly maintenance/security attestation fee of USD 1,000–2,000 depending on scope (audit frequency, rotation automation). If the customer wants 30-day logs (reduced retention), there is an engineering cost (work to purge and adjust metric retention) we estimate at a one-time USD 6,000.

If MiraHealth accepts the BYOK technical model, we'll schedule an onboarding slot (capacity dependent) — procurement, is that acceptable?

Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
